title: P0: Hosted API - Blobstore metadata regen cascade (postmortem)
content:
Executive summary:

On 2029-04-07 between 03:12 - 04:20 UTC we experienced a P0 outage impacting Hosted API request success and tail latency. Symptoms: p95/p99 generation latency jumped ~6x, and our 5xx rate for generation endpoints rose from baseline 0.1% to 12%. Streaming sessions were frequently terminated mid-response. The incident originated from an unexpectedly aggressive metadata re-generation job against our blobstore metadata service (blobmeta), which saturated blobmeta CPU and caused increased tail latency for synchronous metadata reads used by the serving runtime. That in turn caused request queuing in the worker pool and cascading timeouts and 5xx responses.

Impact:
- Duration: ~68 minutes of elevated error/latency with partial recovery and follow-up degradation windows until mitigations fully applied.
- Customer visible: increased 5xx and timeouts for hosted API customers (not dedicated/private).
- Internal: alert storm across hosted-api SLO pages, Pager duty escalations, and degraded tracing/sample surface for the serving runtime.
- Approximate requests affected: estimated 28% of requests in the region during the window experienced >1s added latency or error.

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 03:11:49: hosted-api p95 latency alert fires (SRE-ANOM-p95-gen). SRE on-call pager triggers.
- 03:12:05: First customer-reported error thread in #customer-issues (INC-2029-04-07).
- 03:13:20: SRE rotates to incident channel. Initial hypothesis: upstream autoscaler/edge spike.
- 03:18:40: Traces show long blocking on blobmeta.ListPrefix() and blobmeta.GetMetadata() (90th+ duration).
- 03:22:15: Ops runbook step 2 executed: scale serving workers + deploy emergency config to raise request timeouts from 10s -> 20s to reduce churn (temporary).
- 03:28:51: Found a scheduled metadata-regeneration job kicked off at 03:10 by infra/cron (job id: blobmeta-regen-2029-04-07-03). This job iterated prefixes and triggered synchronous writes to blobmeta that were CPU-heavy.
- 03:34:00: Disabled the regeneration job and throttled its job queue. Partial recovery observed within 6–8 minutes.
- 03:45:00: Serving runtime revert deployed to switch metadata reads to cached path when available (hotfix).
- 04:20:00: Incident declared mitigated. Monitoring continued for regressions until 08:00.

Root cause (summary):
- A nightly metadata re-generation job (blobmeta-regen) was modified in March to perform deeper consistency checks (recursive prefix validation) and was scheduled to run across all buckets. The change increased per-item CPU and made the job issue a large number of synchronous read/write RPCs against blobmeta.
- Blobmeta does not enforce backpressure or request-rate shaping for internal maintenance jobs; the regen job consumed available blobmeta CPU and worker threads, increasing request latency for realtime serving reads.
- The serving runtime makes synchronous blobmeta calls in the fast path for certain cache misses (cold prefixes). Under normal load these are fast; under blobmeta saturation they blocked worker threads and increased request queueing, reaching request queue limits and triggering timeouts/5xx.
- Additional contributing factor: an autoscaler smoothing policy for blobmeta scaled based on 5m CPU averages, too slow to respond to a short burst from the regen. There was no circuit breaker on the serving runtime to fall back to a degraded cached-only mode.

Why previous mitigations did not prevent the outage:
- The regen job was set as low-priority but still had equal access to blobmeta resources (no admission control).
- No synthetic monitoring had a detector for internal job-induced backpressure on blobmeta; alerts only monitored external read latency which trended up after saturation began.
- Serving runtime lacked fast failover for metadata reads (no async fallback or cached-only path configured by default).

Immediate mitigations performed during incident:
- Disabled blobmeta-regen job and drained its work queue (03:34).
- Applied temporary serving runtime config: increase request timeouts and expand worker pool (03:22, followed by hotfix rollback at 03:45 when cache fallback deployed).
- Deployed hotfix to prefer cached metadata path for serving runtime on cache hit; introduce in-process soft-circuit for blobmeta requests taking >250ms to avoid long blocking (03:45).
- Manually escalated blobmeta hosts to temporary scale-up via emergency capacity (03:30).

Long-term fixes and rationale:
1) Job-level admission control: add tenant-aware rate limiting for maintenance jobs (blobmeta-regen) so internal jobs cannot saturate production traffic. (owner: Morgan Lee, due: 2029-04-21)
2) Service-side backpressure & circuit breakers: blobmeta should expose a token bucket and return 429 when maintenance jobs exceed safe thresholds; serving runtime should treat 429 as degradable and use cached-only path. (owner: Ravi Patel, due: 2029-04-14)
3) Async metadata reads and non-blocking worker model: change hot path in serving runtime to issue metadata reads off the request-critical worker threads; fall back to cached data or best-effort partial response. (owner: Kai Nakamura, due: 2029-05-05)
4) Regen job changes: change blobmeta-regen from synchronous writes per-prefix to batched operations with backoff, and run in staggered windows rather than whole-cluster sweep. (owner: Sofia Alvarez, due: 2029-04-18)
5) Alerting & synthetic: add canaries that run internal-job stress tests and detect when maintenance traffic impacts external p95 latency; add an alert for job-to-external latency delta > 3x. (owner: Avery Chen, due: 2029-04-14)
6) Autoscaler tuning: reduce scale-up window for blobmeta to 30s responsiveness for CPU spikes, and add burst capacity pool reserved for critical external traffic. (owner: infra-auto-team, due: 2029-04-28)

Action items (concrete):
- [Avery] Draft and ship job admission-control RFC (due 2029-04-14).
- [Morgan] Implement per-job rate-limit tokens + dashboard showing job consumption vs external traffic (due 2029-04-21).
- [Ravi] Implement 429 path and update serving runtime behavior to degrade gracefully on 429/timeout (PR + tests: SRE-4312) (due 2029-04-14).
- [Kai] Refactor serving runtime metadata access to async path and add non-blocking worker pool fallback (prototype due 2029-04-11, rollout phase due 2029-05-05).
- [Sofia] Rework regen job to use batched updates with jittered windows; schedule via job-scheduler throttler (due 2029-04-18).
- [SRE] Update incident runbook with new checklist: detect regen jobs, immediate disable steps, circuit-breaker activation (due 2029-04-12).
- [Monitoring] Add synthetic and delta alert for internal job impact (Avery, due 2029-04-14).

Runbook updates (to be applied immediately):
- New runbook section "blobmeta maintenance-induced pressure": steps to identify running regen jobs, quick disable, and emergency scale guidelines.
- Add a play to prefer cached metadata path in serving runtime when blobmeta latency >250ms for >30s.
- Add a post-deployment check: if any metadata-maintenance job is altered, schedule a controlled canary run during low-traffic windows.

Post-incident notes & open questions:
- We observed degraded tracing fidelity in the 03:16-03:40 window; need to confirm whether tracing agent contributed to CPU on blobmeta hosts. (open: monitoring team, due 2029-04-12)
- How did the regen job change land without a preflight canary? Need to enforce change process for infra cron jobs. (owner: infra-ops)
- Consider a dedicated control-plane quota for maintenance jobs across all services to avoid single-service saturation. (design discussion scheduled 2029-04-09)

Customer communications:
- On 2029-04-07 12:15 PDT the customer-facing incident summary was posted to status.redwood.ai and emailed to customers with active incidents in region. The message explained root cause (internal maintenance job), mitigation steps taken, and planned action items.

Appendix: brief technical diagnostics and observations:
- Blobmeta CPU profile during peak showed 72% time in recursive prefix validation code path (the exact function: PrefixConsistency.checkRecursive()).
- Serving runtime stacks showed worker threads blocked on rpcClient.call(blobmeta.GetMetadata) with thread sleep times >2s at p99.
- Autoscaler logs: scaling decision delayed due to 5m smoothing window; scale-up triggered at 03:40 but resource pressure had already cascaded.

Lessons learned (short):
- Internal maintenance jobs must be treated as first-class tenants with quotas and admission control.
- Fast-path synchronous dependencies in serving code are high-risk; prefer async approaches or circuit breakers to maintain availability.
- Alerts must surface cause signals (internal job spikes) not just downstream effects.

Acknowledgements:
- On-call responders: Ravi, Morgan, Kai. Infra support: Sofia. Pager rotation: Lydia (first responder), Ravi (lead).

Status: final postmortem; action items added to JIRA (SRE-4312 family).

If you have questions or want a run-through of the hotfix code, ping the incident channel Slack reference: #sre-incident-2029-04-07.
